Title: Query domains and models via the API
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/api-documentation/query-models-via-the-api
Content: When you query via the API, you must use the Data Domain query language (DQL) to fill in the "query" parameter, not the query language you use inside the Model Viewer.

In a single request, you can run a query against either a Data Domain, which includes all lineage models published to the domain, or a set of one or more models, but not both. 

Endpoint

The endpoint is the same whether you query a domain or a set of models:

POST your-solidatus-url/api/vBeta/search/query/entities

Replace your-solidatus-url with the url of your Solidatus environment, e.g. https://demo.solidatus.com

At minimum, a query request must contain the query to be executed and the ID of the domain or models against which the query is to be executed.

Minimal request body for querying a domain:

{
    "query": "Name=\"customer_id\"",
    "domainId": "692d79691249de893f35f785"
}

Minimal request body for querying models:

{
    "query": "Property:\"DQ Score\"=\"fail\"",
    "modelIds": ["65f186936918f9a904fb908f", "6911b078033dbd7092eb30af"]
}

Complete curl command:

curl -X POST \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  --data '{
    "query": "Name=\"customer_data\"",
    "domainId": ["65f186936918f9a904fb908f"]
  }' \
  https://your-solidatus-url/api/vBeta/search/query/entities

You can also create a file with the JSON body of the request to reference in the curl command:

Create a file using a text-editor with the JSON request body
Save the file as a JSON file (e.g., “query.json”)
From the command line, navigate to the folder containing your file and execute the curl command, referencing the file in the --data parameter (e.g. --data @query.json \)
Title: Domain query language reference
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/data-domains/explore-data-domains/query-data-domains
Content: This page serves as a comprehensive reference for the Domain query language (DQL).

It includes a user interface guide, a detailed reference on available predicates and query syntax, and examples to help you construct effective queries.

Solidatus has two query languages: the Domain query language explained here and the Model query language explained in the Models query language reference.

Models query language
For querying inside the Model Viewer, for grid reports, and for filters and display rules in the Model Viewer.
Domain query language
For queries in Data Domains, Data Map display rules, Analytics reports, and querying domains or models via the API.

Note that you can query individual models via the API, but only using the Domain query language.
